info.title: Kimlik API
info.description: The Management API manages the users, organizations, access and clients of a Kimlik installation; calls take an access token for the `kimlik` scope, issued to a service client or an administrator, carrying the permission each operation names. The Account API under `/me` acts for the signed-in user. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable, machine-readable `code`.

post.summary: Set up an organization's identity provider
post.description:
Kimlik discovers the provider's endpoints from its issuer and signs in over OpenID Connect; register `{PublicUrl}/signin/sso/callback` as the redirect URI there. While the connection is enabled, people with an address in its domains sign in only through it. A connection can sign in anyone with an address in its domains, administrators included, so changing connections also takes every installation-wide system permission.

Requires the `kimlik.organizations:write` permission.

403.description: Forbidden

ApiKeyResponse.description:
An API key, without its secret. It belongs to either a user or an organization; `Prefix` is the start of the
secret, to recognize the key by.

ApiKeyVerificationResponse.description:
What a resource server needs to know about an API key it was given. An unknown, expired or revoked key, or the key
of a user who cannot sign in, is not `Active`, and nothing else is said about it. `Permissions` are what
the key may do now: for a user's key, its permissions that the user still holds; for an organization's key, its
permissions. `Plan` is the key of the owner's plan, as in the `plan` claim of tokens, and
`CustomEntitlements` says, as the `custom_entitlements` claim does, that the owner's subscription has add-ons
or overrides.

ApiResourceResponse.description:
An API protected by Kimlik tokens. Clients request its `scope`; the access tokens they get name its
`audience`, which the API checks. The system resource `kimlik` is Kimlik's own API.

AuditEventResponse.description:
A security-relevant action. `action` reads `resource.past_tense_verb`, such as `user.suspended`.
People are referenced by ID only, so the trail outlives their personal data.

AuthenticatorCodeRequest.description: A code from the authenticator app, proving the request comes from someone holding it.

AuthenticatorSetupResponse.description:
A new authenticator key. Add it to an authenticator app, by scanning `otpAuthUri` as a QR code or typing
`secret`, then confirm with a code from the app.

ClientResponse.description:
An application that requests tokens. `scopes` are what it may request; `roles` are the global
roles of a service client.
A web or service client with `jsonWebKeySet` authenticates with those keys (`private_key_jwt`) instead of a secret.

ClientSecretResponse.description:
A new client secret, shown only this once. The previous secret stops working at `previousSecretExpiresAt`, or at
once without it, and keys the client authenticated with stop working at once.

ClientType.description: The kind of application, which decides how it gets tokens.

permissions.description: Permissions of the application that the key may use; its creator must hold them.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working; it does not expire when omitted.

scope.description:
The scope clients request, such as `orders`: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `:`, `_` and
`-`, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed later.

audience.description: The `aud` of the access tokens, such as `orders-api` or a URL; the scope when omitted. It cannot be changed later.

displayName.description: Shown to users on the consent screen, such as "Manage your orders".

clientId.description: Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, such as `web` or `billing-worker`. It cannot be changed later.

firstParty.description: First-party apps are your own and skip the consent screen; third-party apps ask users for consent.

redirectUris.description: Where users return after signing in; required for apps that sign users in, and matched exactly.

postLogoutRedirectUris.description: Where users may return after signing out.

scopes.description:
What the client may request: `openid`, `profile`, `email` and `offline_access` for apps
that sign users in, and the scopes of API resources.

roles.description: Keys of the global roles of a service client.

requireOrganization.description:
Whether every sign-in happens in an organization. When the authorization request names none, the user
chooses one of theirs.

requirePushedAuthorization.description:
Whether the client must push its authorization requests to `/connect/par` (RFC 9126) and send the browser
with only the `request_uri` it gets back, so no authorization parameter travels through the browser.

oneOf.description:
For a web or service client that authenticates with keys rather than a secret (`private_key_jwt`, RFC 7523):
a JWK Set of up to 10 public signing keys, RSA of 2048 bits or more or EC on P-256, P-384 or P-521. Such a client
gets no secret: it signs each request's assertion with one of the keys, typed `client-authentication+jwt` and
with Kimlik's issuer as its audience.

allowTokenExchange.description:
Whether a web or service client may exchange users' access tokens for tokens to other APIs (RFC 8693), to call
them on the users' behalf.

backChannelLogoutUri.description:
Where a web client receives logout tokens when the user's session ends (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0):
HTTPS, or HTTP on localhost.

CreatedApiKeyResponse.description: A new API key with its secret `Key`, which is shown only this once. Callers send it as `Authorization: Bearer kmk_…`.

CreatedClientResponse.description: A new client and, for web and service clients without keys, its secret. The secret is shown only this once.

CreatedWebhookEndpointResponse.description: A new endpoint and the secret that signs its deliveries, which is shown only this once.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, such as `max_projects`. It cannot be changed later.

metered.description:
Whether a limit counts use a month, such as API calls, which backends report through the usage API; it cannot be
changed later.

roles.description: Keys of the organization roles the invited user gets on joining.

slug.description: Up to 64 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, such as `acme`.

pictureUrl.description: A logo or other image of the organization, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

CreateMyOrganizationRequest.description: An organization the signed-in user creates; metadata is the application's, so only the Management API sets it.

slug.description: Up to 64 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, such as `acme`.

pictureUrl.description: A logo or other image of the organization, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

oneOf.description: A JSON object of up to 8 KB that members can read too.
A JSON object of up to 8 KB for the application's backend only.

key.description: `resource:action` in lowercase, such as `invoices:read`. It cannot be changed later.
Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, such as `pro`. It cannot be changed later.

features.description: Feature values by key, such as `{ "export_pdf": true, "max_projects": 3 }`. Features left out are off, or zero.

kind.description: A base plan, or an add-on; it cannot be changed later.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed later.

name.description: A name for people, such as `Acme Entra ID`.

protocol.description: OpenID Connect, by default, or SAML; it cannot change later.

issuer.description:
For OpenID Connect, the provider's issuer URL, from which Kimlik discovers its endpoints and keys, such as
`https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0` or `https://acme.okta.com`. For SAML, the provider's
entity ID.

clientId.description:
OpenID Connect only: Kimlik's client ID at the provider, where `{PublicUrl}/signin/sso/callback` is its
redirect URI.

signOnUrl.description: SAML only: where the provider takes authentication requests, with the HTTP-Redirect binding.

certificate.description: SAML only: the certificate the provider signs with, in PEM or base64.

domains.description: The email domains whose addresses the provider signs in, such as `acme.com`; each in one connection at most.

trialEndsAt.description: When a trial ends; the subscription is trialing until then.

currentPeriodEnd.description: When the paid period ends; omit it for a subscription without an end.

externalReference.description: The subscription's ID in the billing system.

addOns.description: Add-ons by key, with the quantity of each, such as `{ "extra-seats": 3 }`.

featureOverrides.description:
Feature values of the subscriber's own, in the form of plan values, such as `{ "max_projects": 50 }`; they
win over the plan and the add-ons.

locale.description: Preferred language as a BCP 47 tag, such as `tr` or `en`.

pictureUrl.description: An image of the user, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.

timeZone.description: The user's time zone as an IANA name, such as `Europe/Istanbul`.

emailVerified.description: Marks the address as verified, for example when it was verified by another system.

oneOf.description: A JSON object of up to 8 KB that the user can read too.
A JSON object of up to 8 KB for the application's backend only.

CreateUserRequest.description: Creates a user. Without a password, the user sets one through the password reset flow.

url.description: An HTTPS URL; plain HTTP only for `localhost`, for development.

eventTypes.description: The events to send; all of them when omitted or empty.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: Deleting the account takes the password, so a stolen token alone cannot do it.

EntitlementsResponse.description:
What a user or an organization is entitled to: the plan in effect, from its current subscription or the default
plan, and the value of every feature, with the subscription's add-ons and overrides. `plan` is
`null` when there is neither.

FeatureResponse.description: An entitlement the application defines; plans set a value for it.

InvitationResponse.description: An invitation to join an organization, sent by email. Accepting it adds the roles to the new member.

MemberResponse.description: A member of an organization and the organization roles they hold there.

MyInvitationResponse.description: A pending invitation to the signed-in user's verified email address.

MyOrganizationResponse.description:
An organization the signed-in user belongs to, with their roles and permissions in it, and the public metadata
that the application keeps about it.

OrganizationResponse.description:
A group of users, such as a company, workspace or team. Clients may name it by ID or slug. Metadata is what the
application keeps about it: members can read the public metadata through the Account API, and only the Management
API reads the private metadata.

by a password manager or the device's platform, and work on the user's other devices too.

PermissionResponse.description: A permission. System permissions (`kimlik.*`) guard Kimlik itself and cannot be changed.

PersonalDataExport.description:
What Kimlik holds about a user, for their right of access (KVKK article 11, GDPR article 15). `Activity` is the
audit events about the user or by them, newest first; the private metadata is only in exports that administrators
make.

PlanKind.description: What a plan is for: subscribing to, or adding to a subscription.

PlanResponse.description:
A plan and the value of every feature in it: `true` or `false` for boolean features, and a maximum
for limits, where `null` means unlimited.

ProfileResponse.description:
The signed-in user as they see themselves: with the public metadata, but not the private one, and the verified phone
number they sign in with by text message, in E.164.

audience.description: The scope when omitted. It cannot be changed once the API resource exists.

type.description: It cannot be changed once the client exists.

requireOrganization.description: Whether every sign-in happens in an organization.

requirePushedAuthorization.description: Whether the client must push its authorization requests (RFC 9126).

allowTokenExchange.description: Whether a web or service client may exchange users' access tokens for tokens to other APIs (RFC 8693).

backChannelLogoutUri.description: Where a web client receives logout tokens when the user's session ends.

roles.description: Keys of a service client's global roles; when omitted, an existing client keeps its roles.

clientSecret.description:
The secret of a web or service client, at least 16 characters. When omitted, a new client gets a random secret
(regenerate it through the API to learn one) and an existing client keeps its secret. Never exported. In a file
applied at startup, `${Some:Setting}` reads the secret from configuration, such as the environment variable
`Some__Setting`.

oneOf.description:
The public keys of a web or service client that authenticates with keys instead of a secret
(`private_key_jwt`): a JWK Set, as in the Management API. When omitted, an existing client keeps its keys.

type.description: It cannot be changed once the feature exists.

metered.description: Whether a limit counts use a month; it cannot be changed once the feature exists.

kind.description: A base plan, or an add-on; it cannot be changed once the plan exists.

features.description:
Feature values by key: `true` or `false`, and a maximum or `null` (unlimited) for limits. Features
left out are off, or zero. When the property is omitted, an existing plan keeps its values.

scope.description: It cannot be changed once the role exists.

permissions.description: Keys of the role's permissions; when omitted, an existing role keeps its permissions.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of the document, for editor completion; ignored by Kimlik.

ProvisioningDocument.description:
The access model of an installation as one document: permissions, roles, features, plans, API resources and clients.
Applying it creates what is missing and updates what differs, and never deletes. Each item is described in
full, except that role permissions, client roles and client secrets are left alone when omitted.

ProvisioningResult.description: What applying a provisioning document changed.

feature.description: The key of a metered limit feature.

enforce.description: Record the use only if the month's use stays within the limit; otherwise `usage.limit_reached`.

idempotencyKey.description: A key of the backend's choosing that makes a retry within a day count once, such as a request ID.

RecordUsageRequest.description: Use of a metered limit, as a backend reports it.

RecoveryCodesResponse.description: Single-use codes for signing in without the authenticator app. They are shown only this once.

keepPreviousSecretForDays.description:
For how many days, up to 30, the previous secret keeps working, so that the client can switch without downtime; 0
ends it at once.

RegenerateClientSecretRequest.description: How to replace a client's secret.

RoleResponse.description: A role and the keys of its permissions. System roles (`kimlik-*`) cannot be changed.

SessionResponse.description: An application the user signed in to, which can get tokens on their behalf until the session is revoked.

SetPermissionsRequest.description: Replaces the permissions of a role.

SetRolesRequest.description: Replaces the global roles of a user or a client.

SsoConnectionResponse.description:
An organization's own identity provider, which signs in the people whose addresses are in its `Domains`, over
OpenID Connect or SAML. While it is enabled, those people sign in only through it. An OpenID Connect connection has a
`ClientId`, whose secret is never returned; a SAML one has the provider's `SignOnUrl` and signing
`Certificate`, and its `Issuer` is the provider's entity ID.

SubscriptionResponse.description:
A user's or an organization's plan over time, as the billing system reports it, with the add-ons it takes, by key
and quantity, and the feature values of its own that override what its plan and add-ons give.

UpdateApiResourceRequest.description: Changes an API resource with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

displayName.description: The new name; a client always has one, so it cannot be cleared.

oneOf.description:
New keys for a web or service client (see JsonObject? CreateClientRequest.JsonWebKeySet), which replace its secret
or its previous keys. They cannot be cleared: generating a new secret replaces them.

backChannelLogoutUri.description: Where a web client receives logout tokens; `null` stops them.

UpdateClientRequest.description:
Changes a client with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value, and `null` empties
a list. Lists are replaced as a whole.

UpdateFeatureRequest.description: Changes a feature with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

slug.description: A new slug; clients that use the old one must switch to it.

pictureUrl.description: A logo or other image of the organization, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL; `null` clears it.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

UpdateMyOrganizationRequest.description:
Changes an organization with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value. Metadata is the
application's, so only the Management API changes it.

slug.description: A new slug; clients that use the old one must switch to it.

pictureUrl.description: A logo or other image of the organization, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL; `null` clears it.

requireMfa.description: Whether signing in to the organization takes a second factor.

oneOf.description: Replaces the public metadata, a JSON object of up to 8 KB; `null` clears it.
Replaces the private metadata, a JSON object of up to 8 KB; `null` clears it.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description: Changes an organization with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value.

UpdatePermissionRequest.description: Changes a permission with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

isArchived.description: Archived plans keep their subscribers but take no new ones.

UpdatePlanRequest.description: Changes a plan with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value; `features` replaces them all.

pictureUrl.description: An image of the user, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL; `null` clears it.

timeZone.description: The user's time zone as an IANA name, such as `Europe/Istanbul`; `null` clears it.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Changes the profile with JSON Merge Patch semantics (RFC 7396): omitted properties keep their value and
`null` clears one. Metadata is the application's, so only the Management API changes it.

name.description: The new name; a role always has one, so it cannot be cleared.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: Changes a role with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears it.

clientSecret.description: A new client secret; the current one stays when omitted.

UpdateSsoConnectionRequest.description: Changes a connection with JSON Merge Patch semantics: omitted properties keep their value.

plan.description: A plan key, to change the plan.

featureOverrides.description: Replaces the feature overrides; `{}` removes them.

UpdateSubscriptionRequest.description:
Changes a subscription with JSON Merge Patch semantics: an omitted property keeps its value and `null` clears
it. Setting `status` to trialing or active resumes a canceled subscription.

pictureUrl.description: An image of the user, as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL; `null` clears it.

timeZone.description: The user's time zone as an IANA name, such as `Europe/Istanbul`; `null` clears it.

oneOf.description: Replaces the public metadata, a JSON object of up to 8 KB; `null` clears it.
Replaces the private metadata, a JSON object of up to 8 KB; `null` clears it.

UpdateUserRequest.description:
Changes the profile with JSON Merge Patch semantics (RFC 7396): omitted properties keep their value and
`null` clears one.

UpdateWebhookEndpointRequest.description: Changes an endpoint with JSON Merge Patch semantics: omitted properties keep their value.

UsageResponse.description:
A subscriber's use of a metered limit in a calendar month, in UTC: `limit` and `remaining` are
`null` when it is unlimited.

provider.description: The provider's name in Kimlik, such as `google`.

providerDisplayName.description: The provider's name for people, such as `Google`.

UserLoginResponse.description: An account at another provider, such as Google, that the user signs in with.

UserResponse.description:
A user. Metadata is what the application keeps about the user: the user can read the public metadata through the
Account API, and only the Management API reads the private metadata.
`phoneNumber` is the verified number the user signs in with by text message, in E.164.

WebhookDeliveryResponse.description:
One event sent to one endpoint, with the outcome of its latest attempt. Every attempt carries the event's ID as
`webhook-id`, so receivers can recognize repeats.

WebhookEndpointResponse.description:
A URL that receives signed events. `EventTypes` lists the events it subscribes to; empty means all of them.
`FailingSince` is set while its deliveries keep failing.

WebhookSecretResponse.description: A new signing secret, which is shown only this once.

Bearer.description: An access token from the token endpoint, for the `kimlik` scope.
